messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity — cluster island-cluster-42 (customer: AcmeFoods) GPU queue growth >95% for 12m, autoscaler failed to add nodes (retries exhausted). Potential customer-impact: cold requests queuing, 503s reported. Paging oncall.
oncall-ingrid: taking this. seeing queue_len spikes and lots of PodPending with reason "NodeCondition:NetworkUnavailable" and warmup timers hitting 10m. is this the private/vpc cluster? @infra-jason can you confirm.
infra-jason: confirmed — island-cluster-42 is a private customer VPC with no public egress. Node bootstrap uses our cluster-init image from mirror-chi (internal). Recent mirror rollout shows higher latency; several nodes stuck on cloud-init waiting for image unpack.
eng-runtime-amy: quick note: autoscaler gives up after 8 failed provisioning attempts by default, then marks pool as unhealthy. Might be hitting that threshold. We have fallback policy but looks disabled for this customer (explicit isolation).
ops-sre: OK immediate mitigation checklist: 1) suspend autoscaler eviction of pending pods? 2) enable cross-region fallback routing to fallback-pool-eu? 3) attempt manual node bake and attach to the pool. Which has highest chance fast?
oncall-ingrid: (1) unsafe. we need to keep customer isolation. (2) fallback is off per contract. So (3) manual bake into same VPC is only non-contract-violating option. @infra-jason can you try manual instance launch with our hardened image and attach to k8s?
infra-jason: launching one now with --user-data pointing to our backup artifact store. cmd: ```aws ec2 run-instances --image-id ami-xyz-backup --subnet subnet-priv-12 --security-group sg-cluster-42 --instance-type p4d.24xlarge --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=cluster,Value=island-cluster-42}]'``` will attach, then kubeadm join via SSM.
deploy-bot: noticed 12:03 deploy to mirror-chi completed an image repack step. Could correlate — roll started 11:56 and finished 12:01.
eng-runtime-amy: that repack bumped image size by ~300MB; with constrained egress it likely pushes nodes over our 10m image-pull budget. We should reduce startup footprint or increase timeout.
oncall-ingrid: we can short-term: 1) increase node warmup timeout in autoscaler to 20m, 2) temporarily set allow_prebake=true for this cluster so infra team can attach prebaked AMIs. Do we have acceptance from product/legal for temporary prebake?
ops-sre: product OK for emergency prebake for AcmeFoods. cust-success-maria please standby to inform customer of manual intervention.
cust-success-maria: on it — prepping holding message to send if we need to route traffic or say we're performing manual maintenance. Will wait for technical green.
infra-jason: manual instance launched, boot logs show cloud-init_progress: stuck at "pulling image layer 6/12" for ~4m. Attempting to switch to backup artifact store via SSM: ```ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --targets Key=instanceids,Values=i-0abc123 --parameters commands=['sed -i "s#mirror-chi#mirror-backup#g" /etc/cluster/image_source && systemctl restart containerd']```.
infra-jason: OK containerd restarted, image pulls resumed, kubelet reports NodeReady after 2m. Joining node to cluster.
oncall-ingrid: good. while that finishes: increase autoscaler retry window and bump max nodes temporarily to allow burst? @eng-runtime-amy which flags to flip without global rollout?
eng-runtime-amy: in autoscaler config for cluster we can set: ```--scale-up-delay=20m --max-node-provisioning-retries=20 --max-nodes=+8``` (we'll patch cluster CRD). Do it for island-cluster-42 only.
ops-sre: patch applied. autoscaler now sees new node and is scheduling pending pods. queue length dropping from 980 -> 120 over 6m.
tzeng: noticing a high rate of prewarming churn: many pods waiting KV-cache priming which slows eviction. Might be exacerbated by isolated network when pods pull model shards. Suggest temporarily reduce prewarm concurrency to 2 for this customer.
oncall-ingrid: applied prewarm concurrency tweak. also routing: set degrade-to-cpu-policy=false (we don't want lower-quality fallbacks automatically), keep quality consistent.
infra-jason: manual bake plan: build prebaked AMI with mirror-backup artifact preloaded and add to image-set for cluster. I'll start AMI creation and shared Packer jobs now. ETA 30m.
eng-runtime-amy: create followup ticket to add a health-check in autoscaler that detects prolonged image-pull stall and routes to alternate artifact store earlier. This should prevent scale stalls.
ops-sre: customer impact assessment: AcmeFoods reported 12:07 two customer requests got 503; after node join 12:18 errors dropped. Estimated customer impact window: 11:56–12:18 (~22m), ~0.03% of their traffic. We'll include that in postmortem.
cust-success-maria: I sent the proactive update at 12:20: "We've applied emergency mitigations and are continuing to monitor — full incident report will follow." Customer acked, low irritation.
oncall-ingrid: final checklist: - confirm queue <10, - prebake AMI in progress, - autoscaler patch reverted to normal policies after prebake validated, - postmortem stub.
ops-sre: queue stable at 4 now. prebake AMI completed at 12:42 (AMI ami-prebaked-42). infra attached new ASG launch template to use prebaked AMI. Rolling nodes will be gradually replaced.
eng-runtime-amy: opened followup issue INFRA-1729: "autoscaler: detect prolonged image-pull stalls, allow artifact fallback & per-customer prebake policy" assign eng-runtime/infra.
oncall-ingrid: handing back to standard oncall rotation. I'll file blameless postmortem. Thanks all.
ops-sre: quick notes for postmortem: root cause = image repack increased startup size + private VPC egress latency -> node warmup exceeded autoscaler retry thresholds. Contrib: per-customer isolation that disabled fallback routing and lack of prebaked AMI. Remediation: prebake AMIs for isolated customers, add autoscaler heuristics, update runbook.
incident-bot: Incident resolved, severity downgraded to low. Incident channel closed.
